query: Amazon investment in Anthropic valuation gain accounting
normalized: accounting amazon anthropic gain investment valuation

output.content:
Amazon’s Anthropic investment is **not accounted for under the equity method**; Amazon records its Anthropic convertible debt as available-for-sale investments at fair value and adjusts its private-company equity investments—primarily including Anthropic—for observable price changes or impairment. [[1]] 

The accounting therefore differs by instrument: unrealized fair-value movements on the **convertible notes** initially run through accumulated other comprehensive income (AOCI), rather than operating profit or net income. [[2]] 

When portions of those notes convert into Anthropic nonvoting preferred shares, Amazon reclassifies the previously accumulated unrealized gain out of AOCI and into **“Other income (expense), net”** in the income statement. [[1]] 

The converted preferred shares are initially recognized at estimated fair value at conversion and subsequently adjusted for observable price changes or impairment, with those Level 3 adjustments recognized in **“Other income (expense), net.”** [[1]] 

Accordingly, the “valuation gain” is generally a **non-cash mark-up**, not proceeds from Amazon selling Anthropic shares; it reflects a new observable transaction or financing valuation for comparable Anthropic securities. [[1]] 

For FY2025, Amazon reported a **$15.2 billion net gain**, primarily attributable to upward valuation adjustments on Anthropic nonvoting preferred stock plus gains recycled from Anthropic convertible notes that converted during the year. [[3]] 

More specifically, FY2025 upward adjustments on private-company equity investments were **$7.7 billion**, primarily from Amazon’s Anthropic preferred stock, while the note-conversion-related AOCI reclassification was **$5.6 billion** through the first nine months of 2025. [[3]] [[1]] 

In Q3 2025 alone, Amazon said Anthropic-related investment gains added **$9.5 billion pre-tax** to non-operating income, comprising a $7.2 billion observable-price adjustment and a $2.3 billion AOCI reclassification associated with converted notes. [[4]] [[1]] 

The effect continued into 2026: in Q1, Amazon recognized approximately **$12.3 billion** of upward adjustment on Anthropic preferred stock and approximately **$4.5 billion** of gains from reclassifying convertible-note amounts into other income, contributing to **$16.8 billion of pre-tax Anthropic investment gains**. [[5]] [[6]] 

For analysis purposes, these gains increase reported pre-tax income and net income but should be separated from Amazon’s operating performance and cash generation, because they are valuation-driven, non-operating, and can reverse if later observable valuations decline or impairment is recognized. [[1]]
